newsitem.title: BULGARIA: No corporate stocks trade in Bulgaria this week.
newsitem.headline: No corporate stocks trade in Bulgaria this week.

text.p: No corporate issues traded on the Bulgarian stock market this week, as brokers and investors focused on more liquid, high yield investments, brokers said.
"Investors keep their eyes on foreign currency due to its good liquidity and high yield amid the current fall of the lev," a broker said.
Treasury paper was also preferred to company stocks because of the low risk involved in their purchase, said the broker.
Bank shares were out of market favour due to the current crisis of confidence in local banks, the broker added.
The Bulgarian lev has kept falling against major currencies on the domestic forex market this week. It traded near 234 to the dollar today, down from 229/230 a week ago.
Three repo deals in treasury paper were struck on the Sofia Stock Exchange where weekly repo turnover rose to 3.539 million levs from 2.707 million levs the week before.
The 13-share Reuter All Bulgaria Stock Index (RABSI) closed at 41.14 points, unchanged from last Friday.
* RABSI calculated on daily basis since February 1, 1994
